text:
anya: Heads-up — seeing a ~3x spike in mTLS handshake failures across eu-west services starting 10:23 UTC. Started right after the RBAC rollforward for the keystore read role. Errors in proxy logs look like: 

anya: ```proxy.log: 2026-03-23T10:24:12Z ERROR tls handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate, verify error: certificate signed by unknown authority```

mike: :eyes: can you paste the exact audit entries from KMS? suspecting a Deny from the new role binding.

anya: Posted a sample from audit: 

anya: ```audit.log: 2026-03-23T10:23:58Z KMS Decrypt denied principal=service-account:svc-cert-rotator@project reason=iamCondition=false action=kms.decrypt resource=projects/keystore/cryptoKeys/edge-key```

kevin: Confirming — RBAC change added a condition that excludes non-prod proxies. If the proxy's service account identity changed (token swap), Decrypt will fail and the rotator can't unwrap keys -> proxies will present stale certs.

jordan: Oncall FYI, this explains the sourcerer alerts we got. Impact: elevated handshake error rate, partial traffic failures for model-serving and ingestion in eu-west.

mike: Quick triage plan: 1) revert the RBAC condition for keystore.decrypt on the canary group, 2) run a targeted KMS allow test for the proxy SA, 3) replay cert rotator job for affected zones. I can do 1 and 2 now.

kevin: Also enable extra audit logging for edge-proxy keystore reads (add label filter) so we can see any retries/latency. Add a short-lived alert for KMS Deny spikes.

certbot: Automated: cert-rotator job for eu-west-1 queued: job-id=rot-20260323-10-31. Will attempt rewrap if KMS allows.

anya: mike, i pasted the exact binding that landed: 

anya: ```yaml
- role: roles/keystore.decrypt
  members:
    - serviceAccount:svc-cert-rotator@project
  condition:
    title: exclude-proxies-from-production
    expression: "request.auth.claims.env != 'prod'"
```

mike: Ah — that condition is inverted for our flow. The rotator runs as prod identity but proxies sometimes present a proxy-impersonation token. I'll revert the condition and redeploy the binding in ~5m.

jordan: Do we need to execute a hotfix on proxies to prefer service account tokens instead of impersonated tokens?

kevin: Short-term no, reverting binding is fastest. Medium-term: add a test to CI that simulates token impersonation + KMS decrypt to catch this. Ticket it.

anya: Also saw TLS config mismatches in some older proxies: `minVersion: TLS1.2` vs our enforced `minVersion: TLS1.3`. That's causing strict-verify fails on fallbacks. Noted as separate remediation.

mike: Revert applied at 10:28 UTC. Ops-bot: created incident INC-20260323-mtls-keystore.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260323-mtls-keystore created by mike. Severity: P2. Channel: #incidents.

certbot: rotator retry started at 10:31, job-id=rot-20260323-10-31, status=running.

anya: After revert, handshake error rate down to normal by 10:36. Correlation checks show KMS Deny counts dropped to baseline. :thumbsup:

jordan: Nice. Follow-ups: 1) CI test for impersonation+KMS, 2) tighten rollout playbook to include quick RBAC revert, 3) reconcile TLS minVersion across edge proxies. I'll open a short postmortem doc.

kevin: I'll own the CI test. mike, can you add the RBAC revert step to the runbook?

mike: Yep. Adding runbook entry and a short automation that can detect and auto-revert if KMS Deny > 10/min for a role.

anya: One vuln/controls note: ensure audit logs for KMS decrypt include the effective principal and any impersonation chain. We almost missed the impersonation angle.

certbot: Automated: rotator job rot-20260323-10-31 completed, status=success, certs rewrapped for 4/4 nodes in eu-west-1.

jordan: Closing thread for now. Postmortem link: https://internal.redwood/pm/INC-20260323-mtls-keystore (will add timeline).
